sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The applicants seek enlargement on bail in FIR No.392 of 2023, under Section 498A, 304B IPC &
Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Shivgarh, District Rae Bareli.
3. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the son of the applicants on 24.02.2018.

Subsequently, on account of harassment in relation to demand of dowry,

sentences.text: the daughter of the informant was killed on 21.09.2023.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that the applicants are mother-in-law and father-in-law aged about 61 and 62 years respectively.

He also draws my attention to the statements of the informant and PW 2 recorded during trial wherein they have not supported the prosecution story and have specifically alleged that the allegations with regard to dowry were made on coercion by the police authorities.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.
5. In view of the said two statements, the applicants, who are senior citizens and have no criminal history and are in custody since 22.09.2023, are entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicants Nirmala Devi and Ramgulam be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on their furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each separately to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicants shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicants shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which they are accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
